title: Capsule Wardrobe Checklist: The Essentials, by Category
h1: Capsule wardrobe checklist: the essentials, category by category
excerpt: A capsule wardrobe checklist of core essentials by category, how to adapt it to your climate and lifestyle, and what not to buy when you start out.
tldr: Most capsule wardrobes start with about a dozen essentials: plain tops, a button-up shirt, a jumper, dark jeans, smart trousers, a smart layer, a weather coat and three or four pairs of shoes. Adjust for your climate and your week, check everything against a two-to-three-colour palette, and buy only what's still missing.
body:
A capsule wardrobe checklist comes down to about a dozen essentials: three to five plain tops, a button-up shirt, a fine jumper, dark jeans, a pair of smarter trousers, a layer that smartens an outfit, a coat for your weather and three or four pairs of shoes. Everything beyond that depends on your climate and how you spend your week.

The list below is gender-neutral and works at any budget. Tick off what you already own before you buy anything; the gaps are often smaller than they look. New to the idea? Start with what a capsule wardrobe is and how to build one.

How to use this checklist

  • Shop your wardrobe first. Go category by category and mark what you own that fits, suits your life and that you'd happily wear this month.
  • Treat core and optional differently. Core pieces cover almost everyone. Optional pieces earn a place only if your week needs them.
  • Read the numbers as ranges. They assume laundry about once a week. For totals by lifestyle, see how many pieces a capsule wardrobe needs.
  • Swap by function. A skirt can do the job of trousers and loafers can replace Chelsea boots. What matters is the role a piece plays, not its name.

If you'd rather build the inventory on your phone: FitWardrobe is our app, and it isn't available yet. You photograph each piece, it tags the type, colour, pattern, season and formality, and you can correct any tag. The early-access list is open.

The capsule wardrobe checklist: core essentials

Here's the whole list at a glance, then the detail by category.

CategoryCoreOptionalTypical number
TopsPlain T-shirts, a button-up shirt, one smarter topLong-sleeve tees, a polo, a colourful or printed top7 to 10
Knitwear and mid-layersA fine jumperCardigan, sweatshirt, quarter-zip, hoodie2 to 3
BottomsDark jeans, smart trousersChinos, a skirt, wide-leg trousers, shorts3 to 5
Dresses, jumpsuits, suitsNoneA dress or jumpsuit, a suit that splits into separates0 to 2
Layers and outerwearA smart layer, a weather coatDenim or utility jacket, rain shell2 to 3
ShoesEveryday trainers, a smarter pairBoots, sandals3 to 5
AccessoriesAn everyday bag, a beltScarf, sunglasses, watch, jewellery3 to 6

Tops

  • Plain T-shirts (3 to 5): white, grey, navy or black, in a fabric heavy enough not to be see-through. These do most of the work.
  • A button-up shirt: a white or light blue oxford or poplin. Tucked into trousers for work, worn open over a T-shirt at the weekend.
  • One smarter top: a second shirt, a knitted polo or a plain blouse that looks right under a blazer.
  • Optional: long-sleeve tees for cooler days, a polo shirt, and one or two tops in your accent colour or a print you love.

Knitwear and mid-layers

  • A fine jumper: merino or cotton, crew or V-neck, in a neutral. It goes over a shirt for the office and over a T-shirt on Saturday.
  • Optional: a cardigan, a grey sweatshirt, a quarter-zip or a hoodie, depending on how casual your week is.

Bottoms

  • Dark jeans: a straight or relaxed cut with no rips. Darker washes dress up more easily.
  • Smart trousers: navy, charcoal, black or stone, in a fabric that doesn't crease the moment you sit down.
  • Optional: chinos, a midi skirt, wide-leg trousers, or shorts for warm months. Pick the ones you'd actually wear.

Dresses, jumpsuits and suits

None of these are essential, but each one is a whole outfit in a single piece, which helps on rushed mornings. A plain dress or jumpsuit that works with trainers and with a blazer is the most flexible. If your work or social life calls for a suit, choose navy or charcoal and make sure the jacket and trousers also work on their own.

Layers and outerwear

  • A smart layer: a blazer, an unstructured jacket, an overshirt or a chore jacket. It turns a T-shirt and jeans into something you could wear to a meeting.
  • A coat for your weather: a trench or mac where it's mild and wet, a wool coat or padded jacket where winters are cold.
  • Optional: a denim or utility jacket, or a packable rain shell.

Shoes

  • Everyday trainers: plain leather or canvas, in white, black or another neutral.
  • A smarter pair: loafers, derbies, Chelsea boots or flats, whichever your workplace and your feet agree on.
  • Optional: weather shoes, such as waterproof boots or sandals, and sports shoes, which most capsule counts leave out.

If a pair pinches in the shop, it will pinch more on day three of a capsule.

Accessories

  • An everyday bag big enough for what you actually carry, in a neutral.
  • A belt that suits your most-worn shoes.
  • Optional: a scarf in your accent colour, sunglasses, a watch, a few pieces of jewellery you wear daily.

Not counted, still needed

Underwear, socks and tights, sleepwear, loungewear you only wear at home, gym kit and swimwear sit outside most capsule counts. Keep enough socks, tights and underwear to get from one wash to the next with two spare. If you wear tights, a few pairs in black plus a shade close to your skin tone, in sheer and opaque weights, cover most outfits.

Pick your colours before you tick boxes

A checklist only works if the pieces go together, and colour does most of that. Choose two or three neutrals and one or two accents, then check each item against them. Three palettes that work:

  • Navy, grey and white, with forest green
  • Black, cream and camel, with burgundy
  • Olive, stone and white, with rust

A quick test: every top in the capsule should work with at least two of your bottoms. Anything that pairs with only one piece is taking up space.

Adapting the checklist to your climate

Hot or humid all year

Swap the jumper for a long-sleeve linen shirt or a light overshirt for air-conditioned rooms, and lean on cotton, linen and other breathable fabrics. You'll change tops more often, so add two or three. Sandals become core shoes, and a light rain jacket replaces the wool coat.

Cold winters

Layers carry the capsule: two or three jumpers, a thermal base layer or two, an insulated coat and waterproof boots. Fewer T-shirts are on show, so trim the tops and spend the space on knitwear.

Four distinct seasons

Keep a year-round core of about 20 to 25 pieces (jeans, trousers, shirts, plain tees, trainers) and swap a smaller seasonal set each spring and autumn: knitwear and boots in one direction, shorts and sandals in the other.

Wet and windy

A properly waterproof coat matters more than a second smart layer. Choose shoes that survive puddles and darker trousers that hide splashes.

Adapting it to your lifestyle

Your weekAdd moreNeed less
Office with a dress codeShirts, smart trousers, a second blazer or a suit, smart shoesCasual tops, sweatshirts
Hybrid or remoteComfortable knitwear, two or three tops that look good on video callsBlazers, formal shoes
StudentCasual tops, a warm layer for cold lecture halls, comfortable shoesSuits, delicate fabrics
Active or outdoors a lotA good waterproof, trainers that handle real mileage, quick-dry fabricsDry-clean-only pieces
Looking after small childrenWashable tops, darker colours, trousers you can kneel inPale trousers, anything delicate
Uniform at workWeekend and evening pieces onlyWork-style shirts and trousers

If your year includes regular dressed-up occasions, such as weddings, religious festivals or performances, keep one or two outfits for them outside your everyday count.

What not to buy for a capsule wardrobe

  • A whole capsule in one go. It's expensive, and you won't know what's missing until you've worn the capsule for a couple of weeks.
  • Trend pieces as core items. Fine as an accent. Risky as your only pair of trousers.
  • Things that only go with one other piece. If you can't name three things you own that it works with, skip it.
  • Clothes for a life you don't have. A third blazer won't create more meetings.
  • Near-duplicates. A fourth white T-shirt when three are fine is a habit, not a gap.
  • Fabrics you won't look after. If you never hand-wash or dry-clean, that silk shirt will stay on the hanger.
  • Sale finds outside your palette. A bargain that matches nothing is still money spent on nothing.

One filter catches most of these: the 30 wears rule. If you can't picture wearing something at least 30 times, leave it in the shop.

Example: a 30-piece capsule for a hybrid week

This is how the checklist might come together for someone who works in an office three days a week in a city with mild winters. Swap any line for its equivalent.

CategoryPiecesCount
Tops4 plain T-shirts, 1 long-sleeve tee, 2 button-up shirts, 1 knitted polo or blouse, 1 printed shirt or top9
Knitwear1 merino jumper, 1 grey sweatshirt, 1 cardigan3
BottomsDark jeans, navy trousers, black trousers, stone chinos or a skirt4
One-pieceA dress, a jumpsuit or a suit1
Layers and outerwearBlazer or overshirt, trench or mac, denim jacket3
ShoesWhite trainers, loafers or flats, Chelsea boots, sandals4
AccessoriesBag, belt, scarf, sunglasses, watch, one piece of everyday jewellery6
Total30

Gym kit, underwear, sleepwear and a wedding outfit sit outside the 30. Methods differ on accessories: Project 333 counts them, many others don't, so drop that row if you prefer a clothes-and-shoes count. For a trip, the same logic shrinks to about a dozen pieces; our travel capsule packing guide shows how.

faq.q: What are the essentials of a capsule wardrobe?
faq.a: The core essentials are three to five plain T-shirts, a button-up shirt, a fine jumper, dark jeans, smart trousers, a smart layer such as a blazer or overshirt, a coat suited to your climate, everyday trainers and a smarter pair of shoes, plus an everyday bag and a belt. Add optional pieces like a skirt, dress, boots or sandals only if your week needs them.

faq.q: What should not be in a capsule wardrobe?
faq.a: Leave out pieces that only go with one other item, trend buys standing in for core pieces, clothes for a life you don't lead, near-duplicates of things you already own, and fabrics you won't care for. Underwear, sleepwear, gym kit and swimwear aren't banned. They're simply kept outside the capsule count.

faq.q: How do I start a capsule wardrobe from scratch?
faq.a: Start with what you already own, even if it's a mixed bag. Pull out the pieces you wear most, pick two or three neutrals that already dominate, and build around those. Then buy one missing essential at a time, usually trousers, a plain top or everyday shoes first, checking that each new piece works with at least three things you have.

faq.q: Do shoes and accessories count in a capsule wardrobe?
faq.a: It depends on the method. Project 333 counts shoes, accessories and jewellery in its 33 items, while many other capsules count shoes but leave bags, belts and jewellery out. Neither is wrong. Pick one rule before you start and keep to it, so your number means the same thing from one season to the next.

faq.q: Is a capsule wardrobe checklist different for men and women?
faq.a: Less than most lists suggest. Everyone needs tops, bottoms, a layer, outerwear and a few pairs of shoes in colours that combine. The differences are in the specific garments: one person's smarter top is a knitted polo, another's is a blouse, and a skirt or dress can stand in for trousers. Choose by function and by what you like wearing.

faq.q: What colours are best for a capsule wardrobe?
faq.a: Two or three neutrals plus one or two accents work for most people. Navy, grey, white, black, cream, camel, olive and stone are common bases because they pair with almost anything. Choose accents you already wear and like, such as green, burgundy or rust. Having a coherent palette matters more than which colours you choose.
